text:
sandeep: FYI we had two partial spot drains in us-west1 this morning that tripped fallback but left KV cache warmups in limbo. Want to formalize a short decision tree + notification playbook so oncall and services react predictably.

zara: +1. Saw the logs — model-serving fell back to smaller instances but some requests errored with `KVCacheMiss` for ~3m. Need a pre-drain grace signal to model-serving.

eli: Can we add a gate that checks active KV usage and queue length before draining? If > X then delay or route to reserved.

maria: Agree. Proposed thresholds: `kv_active_clients > 5` OR `queue_len > 200` should cause controlled drain (no immediate preempt). Otherwise soft-drain.

katie: Drafted notification flow: (1) infractl emits `drain-intent` 10m prior, (2) oncall-bot posts to #eng-oncall and affected service channels, (3) services ack within 5m or infra cancels. Do we want 10m default?

sandeep: 10m seems ok for short jobs, but long KV warmups (model-serving) need 30m. Maybe probe the pod annotation `x.kv.warmup=true` and set 30m if present.

eli: Implementation sketch for infractl: `infractl drain --pool spot-us-west1 --intent --ttl 600` which creates a `drain-intent` event. If pods have `x.kv:warmup`, CLI should pass `--ttl 1800`.

infra-ci: automated check: when drain-intent created, CI will run health probes: `curl /_internal/kv_status` against each service and report `ok|warm|hot`.

zara: Decision tree (quick ASCII):
```
Start -> drain-intent posted -> probe KV status -> if hot -> extend TTL & notify service owners -> schedule reserved fallback OR wait -> if warm -> soft-drain (no eviction) -> if cold -> immediate drain
```

maria: Escalation path: no ack in 5m -> page primary oncall -> no response in 15m -> page infra lead (sandeep) -> no response 30m -> auto-fallback to reserved with capacity-limit 20% of pool. Include Slack thread link and runbook snippet in pages.

katie: Notification templates (short):
`infractl: drain-intent for pool spot-us-west1 at 12:00 UTC (ttl 600). Reply with 'ack' to accept or 'cancel' to stop.`

eli: Add a playbook section for rolling KV checkpoint: command to trigger graceful checkpoint and drain: `kubectl exec -n models $POD -- /app/bin/kv_checkpoint && infractl cordon $NODE && infractl drain-node $NODE --grace 900`.

sandeep: Ops checklist before initiating drain-intent: 1) verify reserved capacity >= 10% 2) check autoscaler headroom 3) ensure slow-start routing enabled for model-serving 4) post drain-intent to affected channels.

zara: Postmortem note: include root cause, capacity delta, and whether autoscaler responded within 5m. Add cost impact estimate for fallback.

maria: I'll add a short section on rollback: `infractl rollback-fallback --pool spot-us-west1 --cutover 5m` which moves traffic back gradually over specified cutover.

katie: I'll put the notification templates + escalation steps into the runbook doc and create a quick checklist card for oncall.

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: runbook review in #eng-infra on Fri 09:00 UTC.

sandeep: Thanks — once katie posts the runbook link here I'll schedule a 30m dry-run this week.

eli: tiny nit: also log `drain-intent` events to BigQuery with `intent_ts, pool, ttl, initiator, kv_state` for postmortems.

zara: Great discussion. After dry-run we should add a metric `drain_safety_score` to the dashboard so SRE can monitor per-pool readiness. :thumbsup:

maria: +1. I'll update the playbook and ping when ready.
